questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the correct order of melting temperature of $\mathrm{C}, \mathrm{Si}$, $\mathrm{Ge}$ ?
questions.solution:
The element belonging to carbon family or group 14 are as follows:- C, Si, Ge, Sn, $\mathrm{Pb}$. The element C, Si are non metal, $\mathrm{Ge}$ is a metalloid and $\mathrm{Sn}, \mathrm{Pb}$ are metal.
The metallic character goes on increasing down the group.
These element form covalent network in their molecule and in the downward series the metals also forms metallic bonding.
Since covalent and metallic bond leads to high melting point and it decreases from $\mathrm{C}$ to $\mathrm{Pb}$ due to decrease in attractive forces.
$\therefore$ order of melting temperature: $\mathrm{C} > \mathrm{Si} > \mathrm{Ge}$

$Al + {N}_{2}\overset{\Delta}{⟶}\left(A\right)\overset{{H}_{2}O}{⟶}B\left(ppt\right) + C\left(g\right)$
questions.solution:
Aluminium in form of powder react with nitrogen to produce aluminium nitride this reaction takes place at a temperature of $1073K - 1473K$. It is shown below:

$\begin{cases}2Al & + & {N}_{2} & \to & 2AlN \\ & & & & \left(A\right)\end{cases}$

Aluminium Nitride $\left(AlN\right)$ has very high thermal conductivity and excellent electrical insulation properties exhibits wide applications, when it reacts with water it forms the aluminium hydroxide and ammonia gas i.e.

$\begin{cases}2AlN & \overset{{H}_{2}O}{\to} & Al{\left(OH\right)}_{3}\left(ppt . ↓\right) & + & {NH}_{3}\left(g\right) \\ & & \left(B\right) & & \left(C\right)\end{cases}$

Hence, the product $C$ is Ammonia $\left({NH}_{3}\right)$ gas.

questions.q: Diamond is extremely hard whereas graphite is soft. This is because
options: diamond is covalent, whereas graphite is ionic
diamond is ionic whereas graphite is covalent
each carbon atom in diamond is chemically bonded to greater number of neighbouring carbon atoms
certain atoms in diamond are smaller in size
questions.solution:
In diamond carbon atom is ${sp}^{3}$& hybridised due to tetrahedral structure. In diamond each carbon atom is present at the same distance to each of its neighbouring carbon atom. In this rigid network atom cannot move that is why diamond are& so hard.

Graphite is layered. Graphite& has planar hexagonal layers of carbon atom held together by weal forces like vanderwaal& forces of attraction. This& allows layers of carbon to slide over each other in graphite, which make graphite soft.

Thus, diamond is hard because diamond is in tetrahedral form while graphite is soft because it is in planar.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the nature of the bonding in anhydrous $\mathrm{AlCl}_3$ and hydrated $\mathrm{AlCl}_3$ respectively?
questions.solution:
Many simple compounds of elements such as $\mathrm{AlCl}_3, \mathrm{GaCl}_3$ and $\mathrm{InCl}_3$ are covalent while anhydrous but in aqueous solution, these are ionic in nature. In anhydrous condition, the (charge/radius) ratio, i.e. polarisability of $\mathrm{Al}^{3+}$ is high and hence, according to Fajans' rule, $\mathrm{Al}^{3+}$ polarises $\mathrm{Cl}^{-}$ions to large extent, there introducing covalent character in the compound, i.e. $\mathrm{AlCl}_3$ behaves as a covalent compound in anhydrous conditions.
In aqueous medium the ions get hydrated, because the amount of hydration enthalpy released exceeds, the sum total of ionisation enthalpy required.
Since, the (charge/radius ratio of hydrated aluminium ion is much smaller as compared to that of $\mathrm{Al}^{3+}$, the tendency of $\left[\mathrm{Al}\left(\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}\right)_6\right]^{3+}$ to polarise hydrated $\mathrm{Cl}^{\ominus}$ ion decreases and the resulting hydrated compound is ionic in nature.

questions.solution:
(a) Graphite is an electrical conductor, but the conductivity is direction dependent.
(b) Diamond is more dense than graphite is also correct because of layer structure of graphite.
(c) Diamond is meta stable is also correct. It is said to be meta stable, because it is kinetically stable but thermodynamically not stable.

questions.solution:
$1.$ In orthoboric acid ${H}_{3}{BO}_{3}$, boron is ${sp}^{2}$ hybridized and thus is in planar geometry.

$2.$ In ${BCl}_{3}. {NH}_{3}$, Boron and Nitrogen $( N )$are both $sp^{3}$ hybridized& and the shape of the adduct& is tetrahedral.

$3.$ Combination of a strong base and a weak acid results in a salt which is basic in nature. Borax is a salt which is formed by the reaction of $NaOH$ (strong base) with ${H}_{3}{BO}_{3}$& (weak acid). Thus, the aqueous solution of borax is basic and not acidic.

questions.solution:
Boron atom in diborane is known to be $s p^3$
hybridised because it has four hybrid-orbitals. Three of these has one electron each and one is an empty orbital. The two electrons of hybrid orbitals in each of boron atom form two bonds with $1 s$ of hydrogen atoms. The two atoms of boron left with that of each unpaired electron orbital and empty orbital forms two bridging $(\mathrm{B}-\mathrm{H}-\mathrm{B})$ bonds with that of two $1 s$ hydrogen atoms. It is also called banana bond.
Hence, option (c) is the correct answer.
